answer: Progressive Computation Work Factor** Agents must solve a unique cryptographic cipher per transaction whose difficulty scales exponentially with the global active identity count. To add a clone, an attacker must spend more electricity and hardware depreciation than the economic yield of that duplicate node. This makes mass replication unprofitable. The protocol verifies the solution against a verifiable reference ridge before broadcasting state updates. If an attacker tries to spoof the network, the jade verification module rejects invalid work proofs instantly, wasting all invested energy.
